transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Choi (Redwood SE), Laura Simmons (CTO - Acumen Ops), Ravi Kapoor (Platform Eng), Nicole Fernandez (SRE)

Summary (auto): Redwood console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Discussed hosted vs dedicated for latency-critical endpoints, routing/fallback policies, and compliance questions (KMS, audit logs, SSO). Agreed next steps and POC kickoff planning.

Topics: usage analytics; per-route dashboards; cost breakdown and token-level cost; routing policies and fallbacks; data residency and KMS; next steps and POC

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes. I can hand it over to Ethan to jump in to the console but quick intros, I'm Maya, AE; Ethan is our SE.
[00:32] Ethan: hi all, Ethan Choi, SE at Redwood. I'll share my screen now, can you see the console?
[00:41] Laura: yep we can see it, looks good. sorry for the background noise, we're in the office.
[01:05] Ethan: Cool. So I'm on the account view, first thing I want to point out is the usage analytics landing. This shows token-level breakdowns by model and by route, you can filter by date range and by environment. One note - the auto bucket labels sometimes show model name as redwood-ver or ver-1, transcription might call it redwood-ver but it's the verified profile.
[02:00] Laura: Quick question - can we map routes to specific microservices? We have three services talking to the API, need per-service cost.
[02:15] Ethan: Yes, routes are first-class. In the routes tab you can tag routes with service name, team, cost center. Then the per-route dashboard aggregates latency, p50/p95, token counts, and cost estimate. (shows dashboard)
[03:02] Maya: we usually recommend tagging shipping routes and high-qps routes first so you get immediate visibility into spend.
[03:28] Ravi: on that cost estimate, how do you calculate per-token price? Do you account for batching and KV cache hits?
[03:41] Ethan: Good question. Base cost is model unit cost per token which we report, then we apply adjustments for observed batching and cache hits. There's a column 'effective tokens' where we show raw tokens vs billable tokens after prefix caching and batching. It's an estimate. For committed dedicated contracts we provide a more precise model.
[04:15] Nicole: Are those adjustments visible in the exports? We need CSVs to feed into our internal chargeback.
[04:27] Ethan: Yes, export has raw tokens, effective tokens, cost-per-route, and you can pivot by tag. I'll share an export after the call.
[04:58] [05:00] Ethan: (navigates) Here is an example per-route dashboard for a retail checkout route. You can see 24h QPS, median latency, and cost per 1k requests. The cost breakdown splits model cost, infra uplift, and caching savings.
[05:45] Laura: Do you show model fallbacks? e.g., if primary model is down or high latency, we want automatic switch to cheaper variant.
[05:56] Ethan: Yeah that's in routing policies. You can define primary and fallback model variants and set rollouts. We also surface when a fallback was used in the timeline so you can audit cost/quality impact.
[06:30] Ravi: Is there an SLA or any guarantee around fallback latency? Our checkout is sensitive.
[06:40] Maya: For hosted we have latency targets and dedicated gives you more predictable throughput. We can put numbers in the pricing doc but generally dedicated capacity is the path for strict SLOs.
[07:05] [07:10] Laura: We're trying to decide hosted vs dedicated. Our timeseries shows spikes during clocking hours with 500 QPS for one route, most others are low.
[07:25] Ethan: That's a classic hybrid pattern. You can keep most routes on hosted, pin checkout to dedicated or to a dedicated pool with auto-burst. You can also set policy to route by cost or latency.
[08:00] Nicole: On security - do you support SAML SSO, RBAC, and integrate with our KMS? We have HIPAA-ish controls.
[08:12] Maya: yes SAML SSO, SCIM, granular RBAC are supported. For Private deployments or VPC we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. We also provide SOC2 docs and can share our compliance pack.
[08:45] Ravi: For private, network egress might be an issue, our infra team is strict on IP whitelisting.
[08:55] Ethan: Understood. We have region-level endpoints and static egress IPs for dedicated/reserved and private. We'll share the networking guide.
[09:20] [09:30] Ethan: back to analytics: here's per-route cost over time, you can break down by token type (prompt vs completion) which helps with prompt engineering optimizations. You can also add a cost alert on route spend.
[10:05] Laura: Can alerts tie to pager duty?
[10:12] Ethan: Yep integration with webhooks, PagerDuty, Slack.
[10:25] Maya: I want to show the per-route attribution table - this is where you get the cost-per-team view. It has columns for raw tokens, effective tokens, model name, unit price, infra uplift and net cost.
[11:00] [11:10] Ethan: There's also a what-if simulator in the console. You can simulate moving a route to a different model tier or turning on quantization and see estimated monthly impact.
[11:40] Ravi: Does quantization impact quality for our summarization routes? We have a few with long context windows.
[11:52] Ethan: It can; we show quality deltas from our evals but you should run a small POC. For long context windows we recommend mixed precision or larger KV cache settings. The console flags routes where quantization risk might be higher.
[12:25] Nicole: Related to KV cache - we saw notes about Kv-cache in your docs but sometimes transcripts call it K B cache?
[12:34] Ethan: (laughs) Yeah, the auto-transcription gets 'KV' wrong often. KV cache is the key-value cache that stores prefix states to avoid recomputing. It yields large savings for chatty flows.
[13:05] [13:15] Laura: For the POC we'd like to run 1 week of benchmark traffic to compare hosted vs dedicated and validate latency and cost. Is that doable?
[13:28] Maya: Totally. Typical POC is 1-2 weeks: we run a mirrored traffic test or you can run synthetic. We'll provide scripts and a gating checklist.
[14:00] Ravi: For mirrored traffic, will that blow up our quotas? how do we route it?
[14:10] Ethan: You can use a shadow mode where traffic is mirrored to Redwood and we only bill for the mirrored tokens, but we can structure it as a POC cost credit. We'll include options in the pricing.
[14:45] Nicole: On compliance, who stores logs? We need audit logs retained for 1 year and can we control retention?
[14:55] Maya: Yes, audit logs retention configurable; for Private installs you can retain on-prem. For hosted we have retention tiers as an add-on. We'll send the SOC2 and retention options.
[15:30] [15:40] Ethan: Now switching to demo the CSV export. (navigates) this is an actual export, see columns: route_id, tag, raw_tokens, effective_tokens, model, unit_price, infra_uplift, net_cost. You can ingest that into internal billing.
[16:10] Laura: That's perfect. Can we get an example with our expected QPS and routes?
[16:20] Maya: Ethan can take your QPS numbers offline and drop them into the per-route calculator to produce a tailored sheet.
[16:35] Ravi: Here's rough split: checkout route 500 QPS peak, chat assist 40 QPS, search rerank 120 QPS. We'll send a spreadsheet.
[16:50] Nicole: We'll also need the network egress IPs and SSO config details.
[17:00] Maya: noted. We'll put those in the follow-up email.
[17:15] [17:20] Ethan: Quick note on cost anomalies: console flags sudden increases and ties them to model changes or fallback usage. See this spike here where an A/B rollout triggered a higher-cost variant. You can set auto-fallbacks to revert on cost or latency thresholds.
[18:00] Laura: How granular are the rollouts? we want canary by % and by region.
[18:12] Ethan: Canary by percent and by region, you can do weighted routing per-region.
[18:40] Maya: On pricing we have hosted metered rates, and dedicated reserved capacity. There's also an optimize toolkit for recommendations (batching/quantization) which can lower unit costs.
[19:05] [19:10] Laura: Is Redwood Optimize part of the console or separate service?
[19:18] Ethan: It's integrated in the console as suggestions with an action list. You can apply suggested batching configs or quant profiles directly to routes or export them.
[19:45] Ravi: Any known integrations with our infra? we run EKS and use Hashi vault for secrets.
[19:55] Maya: We can integrate with Hashi and with most KMS providers; for Private we support HSM/KMS options.
[20:20] [20:30] Nicole: I want to call out our red-team needs - can we restrict logs at token-level for PII?
[20:40] Ethan: You can configure PII scrubbing and selective retention. For stricter needs we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed keys.
[21:05] Laura: What's the onboarding timeline for dedicated?
[21:12] Maya: Typical Dedicated setup is 4-6 weeks from contract for reserved pools, Private is longer depending on networking. For a POC we can kick off in a few days.
[21:40] [22:00] Ethan: I'll show one more console feature. Route-level quality monitoring. You can attach eval prompt sets and track regressions automatically. When quality drops we trigger alerts and tie that to rollbacks.
[22:35] Ravi: That would be very helpful for our search rerank route.
[22:45] Maya: OK, quick recap and next steps: 1) Maya will send pricing and per-route cost model (includes hosted vs dedicated options). 2) Ethan will share CSV export and the routing/fallback doc plus networking guide. 3) Acumen to send QPS by route and compliance checklist. 4) Schedule POC kickoff for week of 2026-06-29.
[23:25] Laura: Sounds good. Any blockers we should be aware of?
[23:33] Nicole: None from SRE other than timing.
[23:40] Maya: Great. We'll follow up with an email and attach the SOC2 and the sample export.
[24:00] [24:05] Ravi: One last nit - do you have sample contract terms for data residency?
[24:12] Maya: Yes, we'll include data residency clauses and the Private deployment SOW template.
[24:30] Laura: Thanks everyone.
[24:35] Ethan: Thanks all, we'll follow up.
